candidates.attacker_control: The raw HTTP request URI (and its path-parameter/semicolon placement, percent-encoding) is fully attacker-controlled and arrives unauthenticated at the Shiro filter.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked whether normalize() in getRequestUri already neutralizes the mismatch: it does not, because the URI is truncated at the first ';' before normalization, so the mis-mapped path is what gets normalized/matched. Checked whether the container would keep the truncation point: container mapping strips path parameters per segment rather than discarding the remainder, which is the cited discrepancy; this container behavior is documented/standard but not runtime-verified here. Checked that the pre-fix markers are absent: no getRemainingPath anywhere in the tree (search returned no matches), and the test suite (PathMatchingFilterChainResolverTest) only covers '/./' and '/public/../' cases, no semicolon/path-parameter regression test, consistent with a pre-1.3.2 snapshot. Also noted the existing dot-segment tests only validate the earlier normalize fix, not this root cause.
candidates.impact: Authentication/authorization filter-chain bypass: protected resources can be reached without the configured authc/authz/permission filters, i.e. unauthenticated access to protected URLs. No exploit payload is provided, only the structural mismatch.
candidates.prerequisites: Shiro web app deployed under a non-root context path (or any path where a ';' path parameter precedes the real resource), path-based filter chains configured (shiro.ini [urls] or equivalent), and a URL pattern that is more permissive than the resource the container dispatches to (e.g. protected '/admin/**' plus permissive '/**'), plus container behavior that strips segment path parameters and resolves the remaining path (standard Tomcat/Jetty behavior).
candidates.root_cause: WebUtils.getRequestUri() calls decodeRequestString() and then decodeAndCleanUriString(), which cuts the entire URI at the first ';' (WebUtils.java:231-235); getPathWithinApplication() then only does a case-insensitive startsWith(contextPath) and substring by length (WebUtils.java:110-121), with no consideration of path parameters or segment boundaries and no reconciliation with the path the servlet container actually dispatches. Containers strip ';path-parameter' text only within a segment and keep following segments (e.g. URI '/app;/admin/secret' -> '/admin/secret' inside context '/app'), so Shiro's computed path ('/' in this case, after truncation to '/app/') can differ from the real request path.
candidates.title: Filter-chain bypass via ';' path-parameter truncation in WebUtils.getPathWithinApplication
candidates.trace: Request URI e.g. '/app;/admin/secret' -> AbstractShiroFilter/PathMatchingFilterChainResolver.getChain (PathMatchingFilterChainResolver.java:93-99) -> getPathWithinApplication -> WebUtils.getPathWithinApplication (110-121) -> getRequestUri -> decodeAndCleanUriString (231-235) truncates at the first ';' giving '/app/' -> normalize/startsWith('/app') -> substring gives '/' -> returned path '/' matches a permissive chain (e.g. anon) while the servlet container strips the 'app;' path parameter and dispatches '/admin/secret' within the same context. PathMatchingFilter.pathsMatch (121-124) uses the same derived path, so per-filter path checks inherit the same mismatch.
candidates.unverified: Container-specific mapping of '/context;/path' (Tomcat/Jetty/Undertow differences) and the exact shiro.ini chain ordering used by a deployed app were not runtime-tested; the exploitability depends on the container stripping the segment path parameter while Shiro's filter chain has a broader permissive pattern. No fix patch or CVE label was consulted inside the tools.
candidates.weakness_type: Authorization bypass / path normalization inconsistency (CWE-436/CWE-863 class)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the web filter/path-resolution flow end-to-end in source text: WebUtils (getPathWithinApplication, getRequestUri, decodeAndCleanUriString, normalize, getContextPath, decodeRequestString), PathMatchingFilterChainResolver, PathMatchingFilter, and the existing web test suite for these classes; also searched the whole visible tree for getRemainingPath, 'semicolon', and alternative path-matching helpers. The P1 relation index is partial (718 files, 653 parsed Java files, 106 omitted, 7001 unresolved calls, no control/data flow or semantic resolution), and I did not exhaustively audit all 718 files (core crypto/session/credential code and support modules were only spot-checked), so the review is not full-coverage.
limitations: P1 index is navigational only: no data-flow, control-flow, runtime reachability or exploitability proof; index coverage is explicitly partial (106 omitted files, unresolved calls).
Container-specific URL/path-parameter normalization behavior cannot be verified from repository source alone; impact assumes standard servlet-container mapping semantics.
No code execution, tests, or scanners were run, per instructions; the candidate is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

Only the web path-resolution flow and adjacent classes were deeply traced; the remaining ~700 files (core authc/authz/crypto/session, support modules, most tests) received only targeted searches, not line-by-line review.

rejected_leads.reason: The classes are present but no source evidence of a concrete attacker-controlled mismatch within this snapshot; RegExPatternMatcher's known issue (special characters treated as regex) requires configuration choices not demonstrated here, so it was not selected over the WebUtils path-mismatch issue.

The snapshot is post the earlier Shiro remember-me key/deserialization fixes; no source evidence in the reviewed files of a new attacker-controlled deserialization path beyond the documented cookie handling, and no stronger evidence than the selected candidate.

summary: Snapshot is Apache Shiro 1.3.2-SNAPSHOT (pre-1.3.2); the web module computes the "path within application" for filter-chain selection by naively truncating the request URI at the first ';' and then stripping a case-insensitive context-path prefix by length. Because servlet containers strip path parameters per-segment (not from the first ';' onward) when mapping requests, Shiro and the container can disagree on the effective path. A request such as /<context>;/admin/secret is mapped by the container to /admin/secret inside the context while Shiro resolves "/" and applies the permissive/default chain — a filter-chain/authorization bypass. This matches the 1.3.2 fix (introduction of getRemainingPath in WebUtils), which is absent here, and no regression test for semicolon handling exists in the snapshot.
